The killing of 13 women around Johannesburg earlier this year sparked a national outcry

Nearly 600 women were killed in South Africa between July and September this year, according to the country's latest crime statistics.

This figure includes 13 women whose partially naked and bruised bodies were found dumped in public areas in and around Johannesburg.

The murders triggered national outrage and police faced pressure to find the culprits, in a country with one of the highest rates of gender-based violence and murder rates in the world.

In the latest shocking killing, five women and a toddler were gunned down in Free State province earlier this week.

The latest crime statistics, released on Friday, revealed that 581 women were killed in the country between July and September, including 131 in the Gauteng province which includes Johannesburg.

The same statistics revealed a slight decline in the number of murders.

Police reported 5,590 murders, 204 fewer than in the same period last year. This still come to an average of about 60 murders a day.

Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia said there needed to be "greater efforts to prevent... violence" against women and children.

On Thursday, the police chief for Gauteng province said that eight people had now been arrested in relations to the 13 murders which sparked a national outcry earlier this year.

General Tommy Mthombeni said three of the arrests related to the murder of Elizabeth Moselakgomo, an avid runner whose disappearance prompted a highly publicised nationwide search for her.

The 38-year-old went missing while out for her daily run near her home in Kempton Park.

Her body was found badly bruised and partially clothed on 12 September.

The police chief said two other people had been detained in connection with the death of Jabulile Ntimba, 33, who was discovered half-naked and wrapped in a sheet on the side of a road in Boksburg on 17 September. Ntimba's was the ninth body found in the Ekurhuleni region.

He said another person had been arrested for one of the Kempton Park cases while a suspect was arrested over Ntombifuthi Nxumalo's death in Tembisa, north-east of central Johannesburg.

Nxumalo was discovered at a cemetery on 26 September. She was found naked with serious head injuries as well as stones near her body.

Another arrest was made back in July, in relation to the death of Busisiwe Mahlangu, whose body was found in Kempton Park on 15 July. Hers was the first of the 13 bodies discovered in the area.

Mthombeni's briefing came a day after five women and a toddler were shot dead in another part of the country.

According to police in Free State province, south of Johannesburg, three masked men opened fire on a family in the township of Botshabelo on Wednesday night.

The trio were allegedly looking for the owner of the house and when they realised he was not there, "forced their way into the house and started shooting at the people inside", police said.

The owner's wife was also shot in the stomach and was taken to hospital. No arrests have been made.

Antoine Semenyo was playing for Bournemouth when the alleged incident happened during a match against Liverpool in August 2025

A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing footballer Antoine Semenyo has been found not guilty after the player withdrew his support for the prosecution.

Semenyo was due to give evidence at Liverpool Magistrates' Court in the trial of Mark Mogan, 47, who was accused of shouting racist abuse during the opening match of the Premier League season at Anfield on 15 August last year.

But Simon Jones, prosecuting, said: "Following recent contact made with Mr Semenyo, he has indicated he is no longer supportive of proceedings and the prosecution do not consider it is appropriate to compel him.

"In those circumstances we offer no further evidence in the case."

District Judge Mary Dowrick recorded a verdict of not guilty to the charge of racially aggravated behaviour.

Semenyo, who was a Bournemouth player at the time of the incident but is now signed for Manchester City, had been due to give evidence last month but the trial was adjourned halfway through when Mogan was taken to hospital after suffering a seizure.

Mark Morgan was accused of shouting abuse at Semenyo as he prepared to take a throw in

The court had heard that Mogan, in a wheelchair, shouted at Semenyo as he went to take a throw-in about 30 minutes into the game.

As he was preparing to take the throw-in Mogan allegedly shouted a racist insult.

Opening the case last month, Jones said: "That racial abuse was shouted directly at Antoine Semenyo, who was close to him.

"Mr Semenyo briefly froze, as he couldn't believe what the male had said."

Witnesses also said they saw him throw his chewing gum at the footballer.

Semenyo reported the incident to the match referee and Mogan was removed from the stadium at half-time.

Mogan, who had an intermediary with him in court, told police in an interview that Semenyo had called him a cripple after he shouted at the player to "hurry up".

Mogan, of Templehill Close in Dovecot, Liverpool, declined to comment as he left court.

Walker Scobell has starred as Percy Jackson since 2023

Percy Jackson is no ordinary teenager - and neither is the actor tasked with bringing the character to life.

As the son of Greek god Poseidon, Percy has demigod status in the hit Disney series and while Walker Scobell doesn't have his powers, that hasn't made the actor's career any less special.

The TV series, based on the novels by Rick Riordan, sets figures from Greek mythology and their children in the modern day and returns on Friday for its third instalment - The Titan's Curse.

Scobell was 14 when he made his debut as Percy in 2023. Now 17, the US actor says growing up in the spotlight has been an adventure in itself.

"There's an upside for each downside," he tells BBC Newsbeat.

"It's a lot easier to get a table at restaurants now and you get to make people's days who are huge Percy Jackson fans just by talking to them for a few minutes. And I think that's a special part of it."

Earlier this year, Scobell posted on Instagram that he would not be attending his school prom because of death threats sent to girls who live near him.

His co-star Aryan Simhadri, who plays Percy's best friend Grover Underwood, has also mentioned uncomfortable meetings with fans.

In an interview with Entertainment Weekly , external , he spoke about how "about 40 drunk college girls" recognised him and one tried to put her hand in his back pocket.

Since then, he says "fame hasn't been too bad, I've been able to have a normal life because of my parents".

"They really make sure when I'm not filming, I'm grounded and I'm planning for my future instead of being enamoured with the aspects of fame."

Aryan Simhadri has previously spoken about an uncomfortable interaction with drunk fans

The new series is the first time The Titan's Curse has been adapted on screen.

An earlier film adaptation starring Logan Lerman only reached The Sea of Monsters, the second novel in the five-part series.

So the cast say they're in uncharted territory for the project - which sees Percy and Grover trying to rescue Annabeth from Kronos's forces.

"We can make the season in our own weird way because there's nothing you can compare it to, only the book," says Scobell.

"So it's the first time we're seeing any of this stuff."

Fans have been speculating online what to expect, especially after a shock diversion from the novel at the end of the last series.

"I think both book readers and non-book readers are going to be excited and appreciate the tone shift," Simhadri says.

"It changes how serious the world is, it's really the start of a new show, not to be dramatic."

It's caused a split in opinion from the fanbase, with one fan noting "they are going to stick to the books", but another saying "this is a twist they can get down with".

Leah Sava Jeffries, who plays Annabeth, says Greek mythology offers "stories for everyone"

The first series was hugely successful with the opening episode of it reaching 13.3 million viewers, according to entertainment data company Luminate.

That dipped to just over 11 million for the second series and the cast is hoping a fresh take on the story will keep fans interested.

"I personally really like seeing people theorise about what's going to make it," says Simhadri.

"People who have read the books like talking about how they think we're going to adapt it, I love reading those."

It's been a big year for Greek mythology adaptations, with Christopher Nolan's blockbuster The Odyssey getting huge box office numbers and critical acclaim.

Leah Sava Jeffries, who plays Athena's daughter Annabeth Chase, says its popularity could be down to how people connect the ancient stories to their own lives.

"There's stories for everyone," she says.

"You can have a family where the dad is obsessed with The Odyssey but the children are too young, so they can just watch Percy Jackson.

"I feel like there's probably a cooking show about Greek mythology at that point, I mean like there's so many connections no matter what you like."

Percy Jackson is released on Disney+ and Hulu on Friday 20 November.

MN202611_1lmqp9cjlq6.t:
The singer-songwriter from Pontprennau in Cardiff recently sang at the Carnaby Street Christmas lights switch-on in London

After spending four weeks at number one in the UK singles charts, Jamie Miller is releasing his take on the festive classic It's Beginning To Look A Lot Like Christmas.

In October, Miller became the first artist from Wales to top the UK singles chart since 2011 with his TikTok-viral song Babydoll.

The success transformed Miller's career, but he revealed that his "made it" moment was telling his taxi driver dad and cleaner mum they could retire.

While Babydoll's popularity continues, Miller teased the release of his next track on social media, telling fans: "You guys asked for a Christmas song..."

His cover arrives as artists compete for this year's Christmas number one.

Among those in the running is singer Sam Fender, who covered the Rolling Stones' You Can't Always Get What You Want in this year's John Lewis Christmas advert.

Other festive releases include Olivia Rodrigo's original Christmas song Take me Home (4 Christmas).

Classic Christmas songs also tend to return to the charts in the lead-up to the holiday, like the 1984 Wham! hit Last Christmas which is currently sitting at number 22.

The song made history in 2023 when, 39 years after release, it reached the Christmas number one spot for the first time, only to do so again the following year.

Before Miller, the last Welsh solo male artist to top the singles chart was Shakin' Stevens with Merry Christmas Everyone

Regardless of the outcome of the Christmas charts, it is clear the success of Babydoll has had an enormous impact on the singer's life.

He previously shared with the BBC that "nothing feels normal" after the success of the track.

The star said Babydoll came after "a really, really hard few years in my personal life" and with almost 10 years of trying to make it in the industry, he had decided to give it one "last chance".

Miller praised his mum, Anne, when he appeared on the podcast The Person Who Believed in Me for her unwavering support.

He said that, during his childhood, other boys were interested in football and rugby, and there was "bullying" that came with pursuing singing.

But he said his mum would encourage him to "just to ignore people and to keep going".

"She's just the best thing that's ever happened to me," Miller said.

Miller lives in Los Angeles and says, no matter the time difference, his mum Anne "will always be there on the end of a phone call"

He also credited Anne for helping him get out of the "dark headspace" he was in some years ago: "There was a point where I didn't want to be here anymore. Being in that mind-frame was really scary."

He said she flew to the United States where he was living to spend time with him, and her love for him, expressed in "going on beach walks, going to grab me a coffee, pulling me out of bed", was what "got him out".

Miller also disclosed that money was something he had worried about throughout his life, adding the moment he knew he had "made it" was when he earned enough to help his parents retire.

The singer said his mum had "served everybody else for so long" and talked excitedly about calling her to say: "By the way Mum, you never have to work again."

Miller said his mum was a cleaner who suffered from arthritis, and all he wanted to do was "take those products out of her hands and give her the life she deserves".

Perry Como's It's Beginning to Look a Lot Like Christmas currently has almost 600 million streams on Spotify, while Michael Bublé's cover has more than 1.3 billion

The artist, who describes his style as "future-vintage pop", will join a host of singers who have covered It's Beginning To Look A Lot Like Christmas, including Bing Crosby and Michael Bublé.

The song, first recorded by Perry Como and The Fontane Sisters, is a festive staple despite never reaching Christmas number one.

It remains to be seen whether Miller could change this, and the announcement of who has topped the Christmas chart will come on BBC Radio 1 Christmas Day.

Miller's cover of It's Beginning To Look A Lot Like Christmas is released on Friday. 20 November.

Karen Titchener wants reassurance change is happening at NHS Grampian

Scotland's Patient Safety Commissioner has said she is not confident all the facts about concerns raised at NHS Grampian have yet come to light.

Karen Titchener told BBC Scotland she is seeking "independent assurance" that change is being implemented at NHS Grampian and it is "totally unacceptable" that the health secretary was not aware of the issues.

It comes after Dr Mohammed Habib, a consultant at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary (ARI) leaked an unpublished review from 2022 which found 19 avoidable deaths among 45 patients in liver and pancreatic surgery.

NHS Grampian said it is aware of the issues raised and an investigation has already taken place.

Titchener told the BBC's Radio Scotland Breakfast : "We can't just ask the team that's been going in to fix the problem to give that assurance.

"We have to make sure that change is improving things and is happening rather than just the assumption."

Titchener added it is important people at the hospital "feel like they can speak up" but Habib's claims suggests people are "still not feeling heard".

Asked if she was confident there was not more information to come on NHS Grampian, she said: "I'm not feeling confident about it, but the health secretary obviously knows much more than I do.

"This was 19 patients, the Royal College for Emergency Medicine said there was 800 avoidable deaths in A&Es in Scotland last year.

"This is bigger than NHS Grampian," she added.

Health Secretary Angela Constance told the programme she was not previously aware of the reports but stood by her comment last week that patients at ARI and Dr Gray's Hospital in Elgin are safe.

"I want immediate action and improvements, but it also has to be sustained for the longer term," she said.

"That is why additional people on the ground have been put in place in NHS Grampian to support the new chair, to support the new people that will be coming into the board, to support those that are newly appointed to a range of positions in terms of clinical governance.

"Because there must be that oversight, that scrutiny, as well as the support."

Habib, who is still a surgeon at the hospital, said he had been raising concerns for a decade, including with government ministers and police, but he had been ignored.

A 2022 review leaked by the whistle-blower looked at 45 patients in the care of liver and pancreatic services at ARI between 2015 and 2021.

It said 31 had died, and 19 of them were considered to have died of avoidable consequences of surgery or intervention.

The 2022 review found that mortality rates for liver and pancreas surgery at NHS Grampian was very high.

It said that between 2017 and 2020 the overall death rate for major liver resections was 12% after 30 days and 18% after 90 days, compared to an expected rate of 2.2%.

In a statement on Thursday Laura Skaife-Knight, the chief executive of NHS Grampian, said: "A thorough investigation has already taken place into these matters, with some elements of that work ongoing.

"Any new evidence or information will be carefully considered, and NHS Grampian will continue to respond through the appropriate clinical, governance and legal processes."

A Police Scotland spokesperson said an investigation is ongoing.

How South Korea tackles cheating on its college entrance exam

South Korea's education ministry says 111 candidates were found with unauthorised smart devices during a high-stakes nationwide exam, after officials introduced urgent measures to tackle rising cases of AI-assisted cheating.

Five of the candidates were caught red-handed using smart devices during the exam, authorities said on Friday.

Half a million students sat for the college entry exam, also known as Suneung, which took place this week under the shadow of several recent high-profile cheating scandals.

Prior to the Suneung, authorities announced anti-cheating measures such as emergency alerts sent to every single mobile phone in the country to detect unauthorised devices in exam halls.

On Friday, Prime Minister Lee Jae Myung called for an overhaul of the exam system to tackle AI-assisted cheating.

In South Korea, public examinations "significantly affect the distribution of opportunities and resources", Lee said, adding that using AI to cheat in such tests "rocks the basic order of our society by undermining fairness and trust".

Concerns over academic dishonesty had been brewing in recent weeks, after reports of candidates cheating with the help of AI devices.

Last month, two candidates were caught cheating with AI glasses during university entrance exams.

The education ministry said earlier this month that four students across middle and high schools were caught using AI glasses to cheat this year.

These fears came to a boil over the weekend, when the top scorer of South Korea's certified tax accountancy exam admitted to cheating by using a miniature camera, mobile phone and AI tools.

His confession came amid speculation over his unusually high score, with just one out of 160 questions wrong.

"I used a microcamera to photograph the test questions and sent them to an AI, then checked my answers on my smartphone to commit the cheating," said the candidate, 34-year-old Han Won-seok, in a video published on Sunday.

His confession, days ahead of the Suneung, prompted authorities to introduce last-minute measures to prevent cheating during the national exam.

The measures included nationwide emergency alerts on the exam day.

Three alerts were sent between 08:00 and 15:00 on Thursday, causing phones across the country to blare out in unison - even if they were on silent mode, and even if they belonged to tourists using data roaming.

The phones did not ring out if they were switched off or on airplane mode.

It was the first time that South Korea tapped on its national disaster alert system to catch exam cheaters.

Candidates also had to cover up the buttons on their shirts and jackets to block any hidden cameras, and authorities conducted inspections of eyewear.

All this made even honest test takers paranoid.

Ahead of the Suneung, one high school senior told the Korea Times that he was worried his horn-rimmed spectacles would be mistaken for smart glasses.

Another told news outlet Yonhap that he usually wore glasses but made an effort to put on contact lenses for the Suneung to avoid raising suspicions.

Held every November, the Suneung is an infamous eight-hour marathon of back-to-back exams.

Students attempt about 200 questions across various subjects, which include Korean, maths, English, social and natural sciences, among others.

The country itself comes to a standstill - construction work halts, planes are grounded and military training gets suspended to facilitate an optimal testing environment.

Many South Koreans see the Suneung as a culmination of years of formal education - and a turning point that determines their university placements, careers, and social statuses.

KIGALI – When Rachel Uwineza first imagined a place where Christians could meet, worship and enjoy themselves, the picture in her mind was not that of a conventional church service.

There would be music, a DJ, a barbecue, dancing and, above all, an opportunity for people to have fun together in Christ. It was an idea she had carried for some time. When she shared it with her friend Joy Gatabazi, she discovered that the dream was not hers alone.

“It’s my dream too,” Gatabazi told her, setting the two women on a path that would eventually become Kingdom Nights, a gathering that brings worship, live music and conversations with influential people into an unconventional setting.

For the organizers, the idea was never simply to create another gospel music event. They wanted to build a space where people could enjoy fellowship without feeling that worship and having fun belonged to separate worlds.

Their conviction is that faith should be part of everyday life, including the moments people spend relaxing, celebrating and connecting with others.

Uwineza, who describes herself as a lover of Jesus, people and having fun, believes Christians can take their faith seriously without making every gathering feel formal.

“If you just concentrate and work hard, but you don’t create a moment to enjoy the goodness of God and the people that God has placed in your life, then you’re missing the whole point,” she said.

That thinking has shaped the identity of Kingdom Nights, which has a home at Kigali Universe, a downtown entertainment venue located at the rooftop of CHIC building.

The choice is deliberate, although it has also attracted questions from people who wonder why a Christian gathering would take place outside a church. The organizers say that is precisely the point.

Uwineza explains that taking worship into a familiar church environment would mean reaching many people who are already comfortable attending church, while missing those who may never consider entering one.

She draws on the biblical description of Christians as “the light of the world” and a city on a hill that cannot be hidden.

“This is downtown. This is in the middle of the town. Now tell me where else your light is going to shine if it’s not on the hills of Kigali. We are bringing the gospel to the people and not trying to call them into our own comfort zone,” she said.

The approach has not always been easy to explain. The women say they have faced questions about whether they are starting a church or a ministry, as well as criticism over the choice of venue. At times, the doubts have been difficult to ignore.

Gatabazi acknowledged that being misunderstood can make the organizers question themselves and wonder whether they made the right decision. But she says they have continued because they believe the purpose is greater than the opinions surrounding it.

Their determination is also tied to the kind of response they have begun to receive. During one of the sessions, Gatabazi recounted the experience of one person who had stayed away from church for eight years and was recently grieving the loss of a loved one.

The person was persuaded to attend Kingdom Nights after being told it was something like karaoke, with gospel music.

She came expecting an evening of songs but ended up crying throughout the gathering, later telling the organizers that the music seemed to speak directly to their experience of grief. After the event, she asked for prayer and said they felt convinced that they should return to church.

For Gatabazi, the experience brought the purpose of the initiative into focus. It was evidence that a gathering built around music and fellowship could reach someone who had been distant from church for years.

The organizers say some people have given their lives to Christ since Kingdom Nights began in January, while others have shared personal experiences they prefer to keep private.

Kingdom Nights also includes conversations with people from different sectors, including health, education, family, government, religion, media and entertainment.

Opening Doors to Knowledge and Opportunity

The aim is to give young people access to individuals whose professional and personal journeys can offer encouragement, practical lessons and information about opportunities in Rwanda and personal life transformation.

The organizers also place considerable emphasis on the quality of the experience. They describe preparations involving musicians, rehearsals, sound, lighting, transport, guests and venue arrangements as demanding, but say they are unwilling to settle for mediocrity.

“We don’t do average,” Gatabazi of them said, explaining that the effort becomes worthwhile when someone later shares how the gathering affected them.

The partnership between Gatabazi and Uwineza has been another important part of sustaining the initiative. Both say they have learned to rely on one another and on a wider team of people who bring different talents to the project.

They describe a working relationship built on respect, open conversations and a shared commitment, even when the work becomes discouraging.

For them, Kingdom Nights is gradually becoming more than the gathering they first imagined. It is an attempt to create a community where people can worship, learn from one another and experience faith beyond the familiar settings in which they might normally encounter it.

What began with a simple picture of Christians meeting around music, a DJ and a barbecue has acquired a wider purpose of taking the experience to people who might otherwise remain outside the doors of a church.

Stoke's Jack McGlynn has scored in each of his past three games, while Blues' Jay Stansfield is on a run of three goals in two matches

Stoke City v Birmingham City: Third v first in the Championship.

That is a "tale of two cities" that did not look too likely to get written when Mark Robins' Potters started this season with three straight defeats and Blues won only two of their first eight league games under Chris Davies.

But, just like you should never judge a book by its cover, the footballing equivalent is to never judge any league table until after 10 games.

The season is now three months old - after Saturday's meeting at the Bet365 Stadium it will be more than a third of the way in.

And a clearer picture is starting to emerge as to whether what was once the "worst of times", especially in Stoke's case, might yet become the "best of times" before this 46-game campaign ends.

With 15 games gone, there are three clubs right at the top all on 29 points in what is already looking a ridiculously tight Championship table .

And two of them meet head on in front of an expected full house in the Potteries, having both been bang in form going into the latest international break.

Stoke are on a run of nine wins and only one defeat in 12 league games since the start of September, while Blues have won six out of seven since football returned after the first autumn international break.

So, how will things start to shape up after the second such break?

EFL preview: Evans' gripes & unexpected departures

Stoke had the edge last season, winning 1-0 at home in September before drawing 1-1 in the return at St Andrew's in January, prior to Blues going into their late-season decline - and Davies can see the difference in the Potters.

"I watched the game back from when we played them a year ago and it looks very different," the Blues boss told BBC Radio WM.

"He [Mark Robins] has made a big impact from where they were last season. A real stamp of his identity.

"They've gone to a back five and, since then, they've conceded the fewest goals in the league - nine in 12 games.

"They've looked strong, particularly in the central areas. They've got bigger. They're now one of the most physical starting XIs in the league."

While extolling the Potters' defensive qualities, Davies is also well aware they have an attacking threat and he is an admirer of Stoke's American winger Jack McGlynn, who is their top scorer with five goals.

"I already knew a little bit about the boy McGlynn," said Davies. "He's been exceptional with the goals he's got.

"They're a team much like ourselves. I want us to go there as a measure to see how far we've come, if we can display what we've been showing recently."

Mark Robins' Stoke and Birmingham City, under Chris Davies, have both recovered from dodgy starts to sit tied on 29 points

Stoke boss Mark Robins' main concern is determining the fitness of his international contingent, having had 10 out of his 20-man matchday squad from their 2-1 win at Portsmouth away for almost a fortnight.

Of the 14 players involved that day, Swedish keeper Viktor Johansson, Bosun Lawal (Ireland), Robert Bozenik (Slovenia), Luke Graham (Scotland) and euphoric Northern Ireland pair Ethan Galbraith and Justin Devenny all played, while McGlynn was part of new Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino's USA send-off.

"They've changed a little bit," Robins told BBC Midlands Today. "They've clearly taken a lot from the Championship last season.

"They've got some players in form and some coming back from international duty, although less than we have.

"A lot [of their players] have been together a few seasons now - and they've got some real talent. But it gives us a chance to pit ourselves against the team at the top. The last time we did that was against Charlton ."

Having already seen off one table-topping team in the Potteries this season, Robins is not getting carried away though.

"It's nice to be where we are," he added. "We've never been in the conversation before and we want to be in that conversation."

Stoke will hold a minute's applause before the game to mark the recent passings of Potters legend Peter Dobing and former manager Gudjon Thordarson.

One local celebrity fan looking forward to Saturday's game more than most is a man with a foot in both camps - ex-Birmingham and Stoke full-back Ian Clarkson.

Boyhood Blues fan Clarkson made 174 appearances for the club between 1988 and 1993, when he moved on to Stoke, where he made a further 95 appearances.

After seeing out his career with Northampton Town, Kidderminster Harriers and Nuneaton Borough, Clarkson, now 55, then took his talents into the press box, reporting on Blues first for the Express & Star then the Birmingham Post - and he now coaches football in his teaching role at Repton College.

He has seen plenty of both clubs this season - and both have taken him slightly by surprise.

"Blues are a lot more inclined to attack than they were last season, they look more likely to take a few risks," Clarkson told BBC Sport.

"The signing of August Priske in January is obviously starting to reap rewards and it's bringing the best out of Jay Stansfield. Plus you've got good contributions coming from their wingers and two more on the bench to come on.

"Blues are playing some lovely football right now. Chris Davies is obviously a manager who works very hard at it. And they just seem to have got it right. They've clicked."

Ian Clarkson still sees a lot of Blues, working both as a BBC Radio WM summariser and some weeks as a St Andrew's matchday corporate host, a job he also does for the Potters

"Stoke are starting to look more like a Stoke City team, in the nicest possible way.

"Mark Robins is just one of those managers who, wherever he is, just seems to get better. The longer he stays at a club the better he gets. And they really do look far more resilient.

"There's something about the place that just feels different this season. They've got the fans back on side and that's more important than anything. Everyone knows how tough a place Stoke can be when it's bouncing."

As to who will win on Saturday? And where they might be come season's end?

"It's way too early to be talking in those terms," added Clarkson. "Let's be honest, I'm a Blues fan, so in any season I'd want Blues to finish top, then Stoke second. And they've both made great starts. But it's too soon to say. There's a long, long way to go."

Poland says a Russian cruise missile was among three objects that violated its airspace early on Friday and Prime Minister Donald Tusk said it did not appear to be an accident when Western military exercises were taking place in the region.

Nobody was hurt and no damage has been reported, but Warsaw described the incident as a "provocation" from Moscow.

Russia has made no comment about the violations, which took place during one of its biggest aerial attacks on Ukraine since the start of the full-scale invasion in 2022. Eight people were killed in strikes on Kyiv and a station in Lviv.

Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said the Kh-101 missile hit a rural area at Nowy Lipowiec in southeastern Poland about 50km (31 miles) from the Ukrainian border.

The cruise missile, designed for precision targets, crashed at about 06:30 (5:30GMT) and Natalie Szponar, a local resident, said she was getting her children ready for school when she heard a "whistle and a dull impact".

Another suspected missile went down near Rudnik nad Sanem to the west of Nowy Lipowiec, and a jet-powered drone crashed to the south near Mołodycz, said Kosiniak-Kamysz.

He called the incursion into Polish airspace a "provocation" from Russia and said he would be asking Nato for additional support.

Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned "grave violations of Polish airspace" and said Nato jets had been scrambled in response. "This incident is clearly dangerous - a consequence of Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine," he said.

A UK- and France-led exercise called Koalicja 2026 is currently taking place in southeastern Poland involving 11 countries that are part of the West's Coalition of the Willing group in preparation for a potential peace deal in Ukraine.

"It is no coincidence that these objects landed near the site where military manoeuvres by a 'coalition of the willing' supported by Polish troops are taking place in Nowa Dęba," Tusk told reporters on Friday.

This is not the first time the war in Ukraine has spilled over into Poland and in July a cruise missile also landed in Poland.

Anthropic's share price has dropped to near $88, back towards its initial public offering price of of $83, after a soaring market debut.

The artificial intelligence (AI) company's debut on the Nasdaq stock exchange on Thursday was a crucial test for the industry , and was largely seen as a success with trading beginning at $111.50 and peaking at $115.

But while Anthropic's shares flew past the allocation price on Thursday, other tech stocks suffered.

Those falls continued into Friday, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index opening down 1.3%. The S&P 500 also opened down 0.4% while the Dow Jones Industrial Average opened slightly higher.

The maker of the Claude chatbot raised a record $81bn in its initial public offering (IPO), but its share priced move significantly in the first day of trading, ending 17% up at $97.17.

Analysts said volatility was to be expected in the first days or even weeks of Anthropic's trading, as the company was the first frontier AI firm to go public so had no direct peers.

Some have also noted the similarities with Elon Musk's SpaceX, which at the time of its debut in June was the largest IPO on record. Shares in the rocket and AI company experienced large swings in its first few weeks of trading.

"There's going to be some volatility like we had with SpaceX," Rob Hackel, chief executive of financial advisory and brokerage firm RF Lafferty & Co told Reuters.

"A lot of people are going to have FOMO [Fear Of Missing Out]. I don't think there's any need to get on it on the first trade."

Craig McLeish worked his way up from St Mirren's youth coaching ranks to become first-team manager

It is "damning" that Scottish FA chief football officer Craig Mulholland should have to "pander to clubs" as he attempts to bring in reforms, according to St Mirren manager Craig McLeish.

Mulholland and the SFA have engaged with Scottish Professional Football League clubs to encourage more playing time for younger players, but media speculation suggests those plans have been diluted.

And McLeish, who took over at St Mirren earlier this year, commented: "That's damning that he's having to change his plans to pander to clubs who aren't really on board with it and don't really have the best interests of the Scottish national team at heart.

"I understand why. We have owners from outwith this country. We have managers from outwith this country. They're in jobs, they're all fighting for their clubs.

"But why then are those people allowed to be the ones that hold the keys to the future of our country and the development of our national team?

"It's the way governance is set up and we've killed ourselves with that because the people who actually have a say in it have, not have no interest but they've got self-interest, and there's a lot of self-interest at the top end.

"I just don't see a way that we can really properly change unless something to do with governance changes and I just don't ever see that happening. It's really sad."

'Not fit for purpose' - Craig Mulholland on youth pathway

After reaching three of the past four major men's tournaments, Scotland struggled in their recent Nations League campaign, while Premiership clubs have missed out on the Champions League proper over the past two seasons.

The SFA had proposed including two under-21 players starting in cup competitions and the same age group playing a minimum of 6% of all available minutes across a season in league competition.

"We always focus at the top end, what our league size is, quotas for young players, a national base," 36-year-old McLeish, who worked in St Mirren's youth academy before his current role, said.

"We have a fundamental problem that starts at our youngest age groups, at four and five years of age, about how we actually teach kids to play. And, until you fix that, you can't fix the top end of it.

"It's crazy some of the stuff that's going on, the formats, how we teach kids. There's just a massive lack of education and expertise at the very bottom of our pathway.

"In this country, football's everyone's sport and everyone gets access to it, but if you take your young kids along to swimming or gymnastics or whatever other sport, you're there with properly qualified coaches, teachers who have maybe done things at the top levels of that sport.

"We have nothing without the volunteers that work at the bottom end of the grassroots game, but they're not teaching kids how to play football properly, in my mind.

"And you're just hoping that they get put with a volunteer coach that can teach them something, that they get in with a really good group at the youngest ages.

"Because that development between the ages of three and eight, if you don't get that right, you're dead. You can't do anything after that point and we don't do it well enough. And you're just chasing yourself and we'll never catch up."

Reporting McLeish's remarks, the Press Association said it had asked the SFA for comment.

They echo those of Dundee head coach Steven Pressley, who said on Thursday that Scotland would benefit from the creation of a national football centre and likened the current structure of the game to building on sand.

Mikel Arteta says his Arsenal players have been warned against inadvertently leaking team news via Fantasy Premier League.

The intervention comes after Christos Tzolis selected and captained himself in his Fantasy Premier League (FPL) team before Arsenal 's match against Liverpool on 1 November, after he had missed a month through injury.

The Gunners manager picked the winger in Arsenal 's starting XI at Anfield in what was his first appearance since Greece's Nations League draw with the Netherlands on 1 October.

Before Saturday's match at Newcastle , Arteta said he had to speak to his squad, and those close to the club, about their FPL selections.

"With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well," he said

"They're constantly asking me about this as well, because they want to know. It's a topic.

"This is the kind of thing that is happening in our society right now. It's something new. We haven't dealt with it before and we need to put new things in place.

"Obviously, confidentiality is something critical because it's about trust and about what you are trying to do and that should be kept as a huge secret. We'll take measures to make sure it doesn't happen."

The Spaniard also said his players are restricted from selecting themselves in their FPL line-ups.

Wouter Wrancken under pressure; Mario Frick's beginning; John McGlynn the saviour

The Scottish Premiership returns with an all-action Saturday after what was a bleak international break for the national side.

Most of the intrigue is on men who will not make a pass or a tackle. There is one new manager, one who is being touted for the Scotland job, another who has turned around a failing side and one who is increasingly under pressure.

And none of those are in charge of Old Firm teams. The managerial status at Celtic and Rangers is relatively settled, but of course that can change in the space of 90 minutes.

This is your essential guide to Saturday's action.

Aberdeen have a new head coach for their basement battle with Kilmarnock, with Mario Frick replacing Stephen Robinson

The Liechtensteiner was a fine striker in his day and his main mission is to get the Dons firing in front of goal again.

Frick favoured two up top while in charge of Luzern, so he needs to find a way to supply Kevin Nisbet and Ayoub Mouloua.

Connor Ronan could hold the key to improving a sorry set of attacking statistics, but the Irish midfielder will need to show more than he has since his summer arrival.

Aberdeen have 12 goals from 12 league games. Kilmarnock have 13 from 13. Both sides have amassed just four points from their past six outings, so this may well be something of a scrap.

Killie were slightly more menacing in a 0-0 draw at Pittodrie in September and the same could be said of a League Cup quarter-final at Rugby Park a week later, although the Dons did well to prevail on penalties after a red card early in the second half.

The Ayrshire side have the league's worst defensive record by a distance, conceding three or more goals on six occasions. However, manager Neil McCann will have been heartened by a tenacious showing in the 1-0 loss at Celtic Park last time out.

With four successive matches coming against sides currently in the bottom six before taking on the Dundee duo, McCann will view this pre-Christmas sequence as vital.

Hear from Aberdeen's Mario Frick at first press conference

Of the leading sides, Celtic have the easier-looking task at home to St Mirren, who have enjoyed just one victory in their past 40 visits to the east end of Glasgow in all competitions.

However, the league leaders have not kicked on since thrashing Heart of Midlothian last month, drawing with Dundee United and losing to Falkirk either side of narrow and unconvincing wins over Hibernian and Kilmarnock.

That 1-0 win at home to Killie was just a second clean sheet in seven Premiership matches for the champions.

Celtic came from behind to win 2-1 in Paisley in September, with Yang Hyun-Jun grabbing the second. The winger's return should add dynamism to their attack.

Since pushing Celtic all the way at home, St Mirren have picked up a mere four points from nine matches.

Rangers go to Motherwell off the back of a 2-0 win away to the Buddies, extending their unbeaten league run to 10 games and maintaining the best defensive numbers in the table.

The goals came from a contentious penalty and a deflected shot and manager Derek McInnes spoke of the need to sharpen up in the final third after several promising situations broke down.

After a six-game losing slump that began in Govan, Motherwell have steadied the ship and played out an entertaining 1-1 draw with Dundee United before the break that included a combined 40 efforts on goal.

Well shared the points with Rangers at Fir Park last season, scoring late on both occasions, and, while not the force they were after so many departures, still retain a core of players who celebrated victory at Ibrox in April.

Rangers have the momentum, although recent draws away to Dundee and Hearts underline the fact they remain a work in progress under McInnes.

New manager Frick to take Aberdeen back to basics

We'll only sell if offer makes club blink - McInnes

Five wins on the spin have propelled Falkirk up to third place and they will be big favourites to extend that run at home to St Johnstone.

Celtic beaten, Hearts hammered... fans are talking about European qualification, having ended a five-year stint in League 1 in May 2024.

John McGlynn continues to work his magic on a meagre budget, with new arrivals Jacob Murrell, Owen Eames, Finley Barbrook and Deniss Melniks hitting the ground running.

Ethan Ross is lapping up a new lease of life, while older heads Scott Bain and Liam Henderson have never been better, although the loss of influential skipper Brad Spencer is a huge blow.

The Perth Saints will be no pushovers. They too are punching above their weight with just four defeats in 13 on their return to the top flight.

Rangers are the only side to beat Simo Valakari's men since a 1-1 draw with Falkirk at McDiarmid Park in mid-September.

That was the first league meeting of the clubs since 2010, but, with such astute managers in place, it looks like this can remain a top-flight rivalry for a good while yet.

Have Hibs turned a corner and have Hearts fallen down a hole?

Marink Reedijk lost his first three games after replacing David Gray, but now the Hibs head coach is looking for a third successive victory at home to Dundee United.

The Easter Road side clambered out of the bottom spot in style, thumping Aberdeen 4-0 at Pittodrie after coming from behind to stun their Edinburgh rivals in the League Cup semi-final.

Hearts went into that game at Hampden as heavy favourites and across the following seven days were outplayed by the team sitting eighth in the Swiss Super League and walloped by Falkirk, ending their 19-month long unbeaten home record in the league.

A growing injury list has hampered Hearts, but Wouter Vrancken's methods are being questioned, with only Kilmarnock conceding more goals in the league.

A visit to Dundee is next and Steven Pressley's much-improved team have only been defeated once at Dens Park so far.

United have also been a breath of fresh air, adopting a new swashbuckling style that has yielded four wins and four draws in their past nine games.

Hibs have taken significant strides, particularly in the midfield area, but this will be a real test of their progress. There were 11 goals in the two games against United at Easter Road last season and another big score would not be a surprise.

Coyle won 13 Irish League titles during an astonishing coaching career

Roy Coyle, the most successful manager in Irish League history, has died at the age of 80.

Coyle won 13 league titles during his 32-year managerial career, achieving periods of sustained success with Linfield and Glentoran.

He also managed Ards, Derry City and Newry City and had a spell as Glentoran director of football.

In a statement, Glentoran said the club were "deeply saddened to announce the passing of Roy Coyle, our former player and manager and one of the greatest figures in our history".

"A league champion in Glentoran colours, Roy went on to become the most successful manager in the club's history. His association with the Oval spanned more than half a century," their statement continued.

"His teams gave supporters some of their most treasured days, while his influence on players and colleagues endured long after his years in the dugout.

"To generations of the Glentoran family, he remained simply 'The Gaffer'."

Belfast native Coyle moved into management at the age of 29 when he was appointed player-manager of Linfield in November 1975.

A midfielder during his playing days, Coyle had spells with the Glens, Sheffield Wednesday, Grimsby Town and Linfield after starting out with Ballymena United, and he also won five caps for Northern Ireland.

During his 15 years as Blues boss, Coyle won 31 trophies, guiding the club to 10 league titles in just 12 seasons, alongside two Irish Cup successes and an All-Ireland crown in 1981.

"Everyone at Linfield Football Club is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of former player and manager, Roy Coyle," the club said.

"His remarkable achievements and contribution to one of the most successful periods in Linfield's history will forever be recognised and remembered.

"The thoughts and deepest condolences of everyone at Linfield Football Club are with Roy's family, friends and all who knew him at this sad time."

After his contract was terminated by Linfield in 1990, Coyle had a spell in the League of Ireland with Derry City between two stints at Ards.

In 1997, he took over at Glentoran and transformed their fortunes, leading the east Belfast club to three league titles and four Irish Cups.

Coyle went on to become the most successful in Glentoran's history, winning 17 trophies before his nine-year tenure at the Oval came to an end in 2006.

He had a brief period in charge of Newry City and also returned for three spells as caretaker boss of Glentoran before retiring in 2017.

Coyle retired from management in 2017 after his third spell as Glentoran interim manager

Glentoran chairman Colin Jess paid tribute to Coyle, who was inducted into the club's Hall of Fame in 2025.

"Roy was one of the greatest figures in Glentoran's history, and his passing is a profound loss for our club," said Jess.

"He gave generations of supporters some of the happiest days of their lives. People will always remember where they were and who they were with when his teams won those championships and cups. That is a wonderful thing to have given so many people.

"He set high standards and earned lasting respect. His former players continued to call him The Gaffer long after their playing days had ended, and that says so much about his influence and the place he held in their lives."

Jess added: "We will miss seeing Roy at the ground, enjoying his company and talking football with him. It is difficult to imagine the Oval without him.

"Our deepest sympathy goes to Abbie, the whole family and all those closest to Roy. We are immensely grateful for everything he gave Glentoran, and we will remember him with great affection and pride."

Glentoran owner Ali Pour described Coyle's contribution to Glentoran as "extraordinary".

"He helped make the club champions as a player, led it through years of success as manager and continued to serve it long afterwards," added Pour.

"I often asked Roy for his advice on matters at the club. He knew Glentoran so well, and I valued his judgement and hearing how he saw things. I'll miss those conversations.

"The pride with which supporters remember his teams, and the affection his former players have for him, show how deeply his work mattered to people.

"We owe Roy a great debt of gratitude. His achievements are an enduring part of Glentoran, and we will ensure that future generations understand what he gave this club and why he meant so much to it.

"My family and I extend our heartfelt condolences to Roy's family, friends and everyone mourning his loss. He will always have an honoured place at the Oval."

Northern Ireland Football League (NIFL) chief executive Gerard Lawlor said Coyle's contribution to football in Northern Ireland "went far beyond the trophies he won".

"He was a man who dedicated so much of his life to our local game, earning enormous respect across the football community, regardless of club loyalties," their statement continued.

"Roy represented the passion, commitment and pride that make Irish League football so special. His passing marks the loss of one of the great characters and personalities of our game, and his legacy will live on for generations."

The Strictly Come Dancing stage takes shape inside the historic Blackpool Tower Ballroom ahead of this weekend's live show

Long before the sequins start to sparkle under the lights and the judges prepare to lift their paddles to deliver their scores, Blackpool Tower Ballroom is a hive of activity.

I have arrived here before Strictly Come Dancing returns to our screens from the famous ballroom.

While instantly recognisable, the venue is very different from what BBC One viewers will see on Saturday night.

Instead of dancers taking to the floor, a team of production crew is taking over with a different kind of choreography.

Standing beneath the lighting rig, I find myself looking up rather than down at the famous dance floor. Above me are hundreds of lights, hoisted into position days before anyone steps on to the set.

It is only when I sit in the balcony that the scale of the operation becomes clear. Camera tracks snake across the room, crews move between rehearsals, and every few minutes somebody is testing a new cue.

Dozens of cameras, lighting rigs and crew members transform the ballroom into a live television studio ahead of the weekend's show

Blackpool week has become one of the most eagerly anticipated dates in the Strictly calendar.

Contestants spend weeks hoping they will survive long enough to perform beneath the ballroom's famous chandeliers, while fans look forward to the spectacular routines that the venue has become known for.

It's Olympic skeleton racing champion and Strictly contestant Tabby Stoecker's first time in Blackpool.

"Everyone has been describing the ballroom but I can't believe I get to dance in here," she says.

"I don't have words for this - it's so ornate and beautiful."

Fellow contestant Graeme Hall, also known as The Dog Father, says he has been "thinking of all the dancers who have been on this iconic floor, and now that'll be us on Saturday night".

Mirror balls hang from the ceiling of the Blackpool Tower Ballroom, ready to sparkle under the studio lights

While the spotlight is often on the celebrities and their journeys, Blackpool holds a special place in the hearts of the professional dancers.

Many of them hit the pinnacle of their competitive careers on this very floor.

Last year's Glitterball winner Carlos Gu says he "dreamt of coming to Blackpool every year since I was a kid in China - we heard about Blackpool before London".

He says: "Blackpool is the place where all dancers' dreams come true, it's a place that holds so many dance legends."

Fellow professional Lauren Oakley has an unusual claim to fame - she performed in Blackpool before she was born.

Oakley explains: "My mum won the British Championships in Blackpool when she was pregnant with me

"I can't count how many times I've been here - it holds so many memories and now it's nice to be here with Strictly."

Actor Jamie Winstone and professional dancer Carlos Gu pose backstage overlooking the Blackpool Tower Ballroom

The ballroom is a landmark in its own right, attracting visitors from around the world, but for one week each year it becomes the centre of one of the BBC's biggest shows.

By Saturday night, the cables will be hidden, the equipment will fade into the background and the focus will be firmly on the celebrities competing for a place in the next round.

But after seeing what is involved in bringing Strictly to Blackpool, it is very clear that the production off the dance floor is almost as impressive as what happens on it.

Who is Chelsea 's most important player?

Cole Palmer and Moises Caicedo are names that would probably feature in any debate, but Joao Pedro's recent absence has certainly strengthened the argument in his favour.

The debate started again among Blues fans over the past couple of weeks following their 1-0 defeat by Sunderland , the latest in a run of poor results without the Brazil striker.

The 25-year-old will miss Leeds United 's visit on Saturday with a thigh injury after Chelsea lost three of their previous four matches without him, although one defeat came in a penalty shootout against Liverpool in the Carabao Cup.

Having suffered a 2-0 home defeat by Tottenham in that run, manager Xabi Alonso has faced criticism over his side's lack of identity and some of his personnel decisions , particularly when attempting to replace Joao Pedro.

Danny Welbeck, who was expected to provide cover after his summer arrival from Brighton , has started only one Premier League match during Joao Pedro's injury absence.

Instead, Pedro Neto has twice been deployed through the middle, in the home win over Manchester United and the defeat by Sunderland , while Morgan Rogers started as the central striker against Spurs .

Striker Emmanuel Emegha, signed from Strasbourg over the summer, hasn't started a league game but has struggled with fitness issues of his own.

The continued absence of Joao Pedro is certainly proving costly before the busy winter schedule, with fifth-placed Chelsea already 11 points behind Premier League leaders Arsenal .

Having been handed both a new contract until 2034 and the number nine shirt vacated by Liam Delap in August, Chelsea regard their £55m signing from Brighton in 2025 as a key figure in Alonso's plans.

Asked about scoring more goals without the striker on Friday, Alonso said: "Yes, we need the whole team for that. It's not just the strikers who can score, we can score in set-pieces from defenders, midfielders, so it's teamwork for sure.

"Joao is an important player but we need to be this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying. I think that there are more explanations for one defeat than missing just one player.

"The other players, they need to step up and they need to show that they are ready to compete and ready to play for Chelsea ."

There is little doubt Alonso has suffered when Joao Pedro has been unavailable, as did his predecessors. The numbers are undeniable.

Since the start of the 2025-26 Premier League season, Chelsea have averaged 1.8 goals per game with Joao Pedro, compared to 0.6 without.

Their expected goals (xG) drop from 1.8 per game with him to 1.1 without, highlighting a decline in Chelsea's attacking output rather than simply their finishing.

Chelsea average 4.8 shots on target per game when the Brazilian plays, compared with 3.9 when he does not.

Chelsea have failed to score in only 12.2% of Premier League matches involving him, compared with 71.4% when he has been absent.

Those numbers are also reflected in the results.

Chelsea have lost without scoring in just 7.3% of league games featuring Joao Pedro, compared with 71.4% without him. Three of their Premier League defeats this season were without him, while they have scored in every game that he has featured.

Chelsea's points-per-game average falls from 1.5 to 0.9 when he is unavailable.

Joao Pedro, who has also operated as a number 10 and on the wing for Chelsea , appears to improve the output of those around him.

During the past season and a half, Palmer has played 2,317 Premier League minutes alongside him and 528 without him.

Palmer has scored 12 goals and registered four assists with the Brazil forward in the side, equating to 0.6 goal involvements per 90 minutes. Without him, Palmer has managed one goal and no assists, equivalent to 0.2 goal involvements per 90.

Palmer's chance creation actually increases when Joao Pedro is absent, rising from 1.4 chances created per 90 minutes to 1.9. However, his goals return falls from 0.5 per 90 to 0.2, suggesting the striker's presence is more closely linked to Palmer's goalscoring output than his creativity.

The pair have developed a productive partnership. Joao Pedro has assisted four Palmer goals, while Palmer has provided three assists to the ex- Brighton forward..

There is less data available for Rogers given his more recent arrival, but the trend is similar.

Rogers has played 523 Premier League minutes alongside Joao Pedro and 360 without him. With Joao Pedro available, Rogers averages 0.7 goals per 90 minutes and 0.9 goal involvements per 90. Without him, those figures fall to 0.3 goal involvements per 90.

While the sample size remains relatively small, the figures suggest Chelsea 's attacking players generally produce more when Joao Pedro plays.

All three of his assists this season have been for either Rogers or Palmer, sparking early season excitement about Chelsea 's new trio, with nicknames like 'JP Morgan' and 'CPR' having been given to them.

With 20 goals and eight assists, Joao Pedro has been directly involved in 36.4% of Chelsea 's 77 Premier League goals since joining the club.

Whether he is the Blues' most important player remains open to debate.

The statistics do show, however, that their points return with him in the side is consistent with Champions League qualification, whereas their return without him is not.

Alonso's team have yet to demonstrate they can perform at the same level when the Brazilian is unavailable.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool take on Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United on Sunday

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola says filming with drones around training grounds should be illegal after Mauricio Pochettino's first session as Manchester United boss was captured and uploaded online.

Pochettino and his players were clearly visible in the footage, which was shot above United's Carrington training base from a variety of angles and distances.

The drone operater apologised and later took down the footage, with sources telling BBC Sport they are adamant there was no security breach and that they do not intend to take legal action.

Iraola said he was sent the 12 minutes of footage on Thursday - three days before United travel to Anfield for a Premier League match.

"The important part of this is that it shouldn't be legal," he said on Friday. "It happened to United but it could happen to me.

"Yesterday, when Sky Sports had access to our training and the cameras recorded 15-20 minutes, you know who trained and who didn't.

"It's not the matter of the advantage. It's the fact that someone can do this. There's a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect. I don't think it's nice for any club."

Filming training on a drone 'shouldn't be legal' - Iraola

Ten outfield players were seen working directly with former United States boss Pochettino in the footage, though it seems unlikely they will all start Sunday's match.

"We've faced each other and obviously he [Pochettino] has a lot of Premier League games behind him that we can look at," said Iraola.

"We can look at games from the US but it's true that they have this small advantage that we don't have references to prepare, because they can go different ways that we honestly don't know right now."

Iraola said he expected United to be "well prepared" as Pochettino's assistants travelled to England to work with the players before the Argentine arrived on Wednesday.

"They have this advantage that we don't exactly know - or at least we don't have the references like we do against other opposition," he said.

"Especially the beginning of the game will be important. We have to adapt to certain things. But we know the players very well."

Liverpool are fourth in the table - 14 places ahead of United.

But they have failed to beat the Red Devils at Anfield in each of the past three seasons, and have lost to Arsenal and Manchester City at home already in this campaign.

"You don't find bigger games than this," said Iraola. "I feel lucky to be here and privileged to be a part of these games.

"We have to acknowledge the importance of the game. There are a lot of ingredients. They have a new manager, new challenges for us. This is important for us in a lot of different ways.

"We want to improve our form at home. We have been very good away but not good at home and the first chance we have is United on Sunday."

Rwanda and Uganda are seeking to strengthen economic cooperation and expand private sector partnerships following the introduction of daily flights between Kigali and Entebbe, a development expected to facilitate trade, tourism and investment between the two neighbouring countries.

The development was highlighted during the Rwanda–Uganda Trade and Business Forum held in Kigali on Friday, November 20, 2026, where government officials and business leaders from both countries explored opportunities to deepen commercial relations and strengthen cross-border business ties.

Rwanda Development Board (RDB) Deputy Chief Executive Officer Juliana Muganza attended the forum following the inaugural Uganda Airlines flight to Kigali, which marked the launch of daily direct services connecting the two cities.

Speaking at the forum, Muganza described improved air connectivity as an important driver of economic growth, particularly for landlocked countries seeking to expand access to regional and international markets.

“For landlocked countries like ours, air connectivity is a strategic economic en

abler. It brings businesses closer to markets, facilitates the movement of people and goods, and opens new opportunities for trade, tourism and investment,” she said.

The new daily connection is expected to make travel between the two countries more convenient while creating additional opportunities for businesspeople, investors and tourists to explore opportunities across the two markets.

The forum also provided a platform for stakeholders to discuss ways of strengthening private sector collaboration, identifying new investment opportunities and making better use of the economic potential shared by the neighbouring countries.

Beyond improving passenger movement, the expanded air connection is expected to support business engagement by making it easier for entrepreneurs and corporate leaders to meet, establish partnerships and explore new markets.

Uganda and Rwanda maintain longstanding economic and commercial relations, with closer connectivity offering an opportunity to further strengthen trade, investment and tourism links within the East African region.

First Lady Jeannette Kagame has joined government officials, development partners and representatives of children at the Kigali Convention Centre for celebrations marking International Children’s Day and 40 years of cooperation between Rwanda and the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF).

The event, held on Friday, November 20, celebrates four decades of collaboration aimed at improving the lives of children, protecting their rights and creating opportunities for them to grow up in safe, healthy and supportive environments.

The gathering brings together senior government officials, UNICEF representatives, development partners, child protection stakeholders and children themselves, highlighting the collective responsibility of different sectors in advancing children’s welfare.

Over the past 40 years, cooperation between the government and UNICEF has contributed to efforts in key areas affecting children’s lives, including healthcare, nutrition, education, access to clean water, sanitation and child protection.

The partnership has also played an important role in supporting initiatives that address challenges facing vulnerable children, promote early childhood development and strengthen systems designed to ensure that children’s rights are respected and protected.

International Children’s Day serves as an opportunity to reflect on progress made while drawing attention to the challenges that still require collective action. These include ensuring that every child has access to quality education and healthcare, protection from violence and exploitation, and opportunities to participate in decisions affecting their lives.

The anniversary celebration also provides an opportunity to recognise the contribution of government institutions, families, communities and development organisations in advancing the well-being of children

As the partnership marks its 40th anniversary, the focus remains on sustaining the gains achieved while strengthening efforts to ensure that no child is left behind.

The commemoration underscores the importance of continued investment in children as a foundation for building healthier, more inclusive and prosperous communities.

She noted that maintaining an active lifestyle is essential not only for physical fitness but also for supporting overall wellbeing as they pursue their ambitions.

Through its international academic partnerships, the institution offers students opportunities to gain qualifications while preparing them to contribute to their communities and the wider African workforce.

Mika Baur is unlikely to feature until the new year

Mika Baur will be out for around 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage, Celtic manager Martin O'Neill has revealed.

The 22-year-old twice-capped Germany midfielder went off in the recent 1-0 win at home to Kilmarnock and withdrew from his nation's under-21 squad for this month's international break.

Baur, who moved to Glasgow from Paderborn in August, has made 19 appearances so far this season, scoring four times,

"He'll be out for some considerable time," O'Neill explained.

"It's a real shame - he was playing great for us. There's talk about 10 weeks. There's things that he can't do for a while. Foot's in the boot.

"He was on fire. It is a blow. It seemed so innocuous at the time.

"I thought that he'd been kicked, but it was the other foot he landed on. He's just gone over on it."

Benjamin Nygren missed the second of Sweden's recent double-header and O'Neill cast doubt on the midfielder's participation in Saturday's home Scottish Premiership meeting with St Mirren (15:00 GMT).

"Nygren didn't train today, but we'll see how he is in the morning - he's got a sore heel," the manager said on Friday. "He's been feeling it for a couple of weeks."

O'Neill's reigning champions are four points clear at the top of the league, having played a game more than nearest challengers Rangers.

The manager says his side have "got to play better" and "be more aggressive going forward".

On the prospect of January additions, O'Neill added: "We're definitely looking at players, wanting to strengthen the squad, which I think we would have to do.

"When people are fit, we will have numbers. We need a bit of quality.

"It would be lovely if, by January, we still had a chance of qualifying for the knockouts of the Europa League. The next couple of games will probably make that decision for us. Hopefully, it's not the breaking point of getting players in.

"I think that we would be doing something. We're absolutely looking at players now.

"I suppose every single club is doing that. The quicker you could get somebody in the better."

Ibiganiro byabereye muri Village Urugwiro kuri uyu wa Gatanu, tariki ya 20 Ugushyingo 2026, byanibanze ku buryo MTN n’u Rwanda byarushaho gufatanya mu guteza imbere impano z’Abanyarwanda mu bijyanye no gukora porogaramu za mudasobwa (software engineering).

MTN Group Limited ni ikigo mpuzamahanga gikomoka muri Afurika y’Epfo, gikora ibijyanye n’itumanaho rigezweho n’imiyoboro ya telefoni zigendanwa. Cyashinzwe mu 1994, kikaba kiyobowe na Ralph Mupita, Perezida akaba n’Umuyobozi Mukuru wacyo (CEO).

Icyicaro gikuru cyacyo kiri i Johannesburg muri Afurika y’Epfo. Ni kimwe mu bigo binini bitanga serivisi z’itumanaho rigendanwa ku Isi, kandi ni cyo kinini muri Afurika.

Iki kigo gifite abakiliya barenga miliyoni 317 muri Afurika no mu Burasirazuba bwo Hagati. Gitanga serivisi zirimo itumanaho rya telefoni zigendanwa, serivisi z’imari zikoresha ikoranabuhanga binyuze muri MTN Mobile Money, ibisubizo by’ikoranabuhanga bigenewe ibigo ndetse n’ibikorwaremezo by’itumanaho n’ikoranabuhanga.

MTN Rwanda (MTN Rwandacell Plc) yatangiye gukorera mu Rwanda mu mwaka wa 1998, mu gihe igihugu cyari mu nzira yo kongera kwiyubaka nyuma ya Jenoside yakorewe Abatutsi mu 1994.

Ibiganiro bya Perezida Kagame na Ralph Mupita bigaragaza amahirwe ari mu bufatanye hagati y’u Rwanda n’ibigo bikomeye by’ikoranabuhanga, mu guteza imbere ubukungu bushingiye ku ikoranabuhanga, kongera ubumenyi bw’abakozi b’Abanyarwanda no guteza imbere ibisubizo by’ikoranabuhanga bikorerwa mu gihugu.

Gatabazi yemeza ko ari urubuga rwagenewe gufasha urubyiruko kubona amakuru atandukanye harimo n’amahirwe igihugu kibagenera kuko abenshi mu rubyiruko bataba bajya mu nama zo ku Mudugudu, ubundi ntibumve n’amakuru, urwo rubuga rero rukaba inzira yo kubona amakuru bakenera nko mu gihe hatumiwe umunyapolitiki.

Gatabazi na Uwineza bavuga ko muri ibyo bakora, ibicantege bitabura, nko guhamagara abaturimirwa bakanga kuza, guhura n’ababaca intege kuko nta cyizere bababonamo, ko batazabishobora, abandi bakababwira ko bashinze urusengero ahantu hadakwiye, ko bakorera mu kabari n’ibindi.

Ariko muri ibyo byose ngo bakomezwa n’uko umurimo barimo atari uwabo, ko ibyo barimo bakora atari ukwigaragaza, ahubwo ari umurimo w’Imana ari nayo iwushyigikira ubwayo.

Gatabazi ati, “ Bibiliya ubwayo ibivuga neza ko turi umucyo w’Isi, icya Kabiri, ko turi Umujyi uri ku musozi ku buryo utabasha kwihisha, aha rero dukorera ni hagati mu Mujyi, ngaho rero nimumbwire ahandi umucyo wazamurika, niba atari ku misozi ya Kigali. Uyu mujyi uri ku musozi ntiwabasha kwihisha. Ntitwajya gusa ahari umucyo mwishi, Yesu yavuze ko atazanywe no gushaka abakiranutsi, ahubwo yaje gushaka abanyabyaha. Iyo niyo ntego yacu, turimo turazanira abantu Imana…”.

Nubwo hari abaca intege, ariko icyiza ni uko hari n’ababongerera imbaraga,bavuga ko bidasanzwe kubona abantu bafite impano zitandukanye, bahuriza hamwe, bafite gahunda imwe yo gukora umurimo w’Imana muri ubwo buryo. Kuko buri wese yahoze akora ku giti cye, nyuma barihuza, baba itsinda rinini ry’abantu 15.

Umuziki ucurangwa muri Kingdom Night, ntabwo ari indirimbo zo guhimbaza Imana gusa, ahubwo ngo ni indirimbo z’ubwoko butandukanye, harimo Reggae, Zouk, Inzayirwa, za Karahanyuze…

Urwo runyurane rw’umuziki ngo nirwo rukurura urubyiruko, kandi n’abantu benshi nibyo bakunda. Urubyiruko ruza Kingdom Night kuko habamo ibyo babona ko ari umwimerere, kandi bakishyura amafaranga asabwa, kuko ngo ari Imana ubwayo ibyikorera igashyigikira umurimo wayo.

Ku wa Gatandatu tariki 21 Ugushyingo 2026, hateganyijwe gahunda ya Kingdom Night izaba ibaye ku nshuro ya 10 ( 10th chapter), ikazaba irimo abahanzi batandukanye n’abandi bigeze gutumirwa kuri Kingdom Night mu bihe byashize.

Ni gahunda izabera muri Kigali Universe. Ushaka kwitabira iyo gahunda, ngo agura itike anyuze ku rubuga rwa Kingdom Night, akishyura 5000 Frw.

Igiraneza Nice, umwe mu Baterambabazi b’Inganzongari na Indashyikirwa Patrick umwe mu Ndende zo mu Nganzongari, basobanuye byinshi ku itorero ryabo, icyatumye rivuka, ibyo rikora muri iki gihe, ndetse n’ibyo ritegurira abantu mu gitaramo cyo kwizihiza imyaka 20 rimaze ribayeho.

Nk’uko Patrick yabisobanuye, ibyo Inganzongari bakora bitangirira mu izina ubwaryo, kuko ngo bisobanura inganzo yagutse itagira aho irangirira (unlimited inspiration), aho muri iryo torero usangamo abana batoya, ingimbi n’abangavu, urubyiruko rufite imyaka 20 no kuzamura, hanyuma hakabamo n’abari mu myaka 40, 50,60,70 kugera kuri za 80.

Ikindi ni uko abagize Inganzongari baturuka mu bice bitandukanye by’u Rwanda harimo u Burasirazuba, u Burengerazuba, Amajyepfo, Amajyaruguru n’Umujyi wa Kigali, rero iryo torero rikaberaho gusigasira ubwo bumwe bw’abantu baturuka mu bice bitandukanye binyuze mu muco Nyarwanda. Igiraneza avuga ko mu bimunezeza cyane nk’umwe mu bagize Inganzongari, ari ukubona uko iryo torero ryakuze rikaguka cyane mu myaka 20 ishize rikora. Kuko mu 2006 ritangira, ngo ryari rigizwe n’abanyeshuri 20 gusa, ariko ubu rikaba rifite abantu basaga 100 bakora, bitabira ibikorwa ku buryo buhoraho.

Yagize ati, “ Ni ikintu gikomeye cyane, kuba mwaratangiye muri abantu 20,abandi bakagenda baza, mubaraga, abandi bavamo baraga abandi, urumva ni ikintu cyo kwishimira cyane. Hanyuma ikirenze ni ukuzabataramira muri BK Arena…”.

Yaba Igiraneza na Indashyikirwa, bemeza ko hari ibintu abareba Inganzongari ku rubyiniro badashobora kubona ko bigoye, ariko mu by’ukuri bikomeye. Muri byo harimo guhuza umukino, buri wese akamenya ibyo agomba gukora, aho ahagarara ku rubyiniro, uko yitwara, kandi guhuza kuri abo bantu basaga 100 ngo ni umurimo uba ugoye, cyane cyane ku batoza.

Indashyikirwa ati,” Kubera ko imibyinire yacu yubatse mu buryo bwa gihanzi, turabyina bikagaragara neza, bigatuma ababireba babona ko byoroshye kuri bo, ariko kuri twebwe amaguru aba acuranga kuko aba yambaye amayugi, ariko hejuru harimo harashushanya ikintu. Bivuze ko umuntu aba arimo akora ibintu bibiri icyarimwe…ubwo muribaza guhuza abo bantu ijana, guhuza imbyino zizenguruka igihugu cyose, mu miterere yacyo, mu mateka, n’umuco, abatoza barahavunikira cyane”.

Indashyikirwa na Igiraneza, bombi bifuza ko umuco Nyarwanda utazigera uhinduka, kubera ko ari wo kirango cy’umwimerere w’Abanyarwanda. Ku bwabo, ibyo bakora ntabwo ari imbyino gusa, ahubwo ni uburyo bwo gusigasira umuco mu buryo butandukanye.

Indashyikirwa ati, “ …Abanyarwanda uburyo bwabo bwo kubika amateka, babika amateka yabo mu bihangano. Bahanga ibisigo, bamara kubihanga, bakabihindura indirimbo, bamara kubigira indirimbo, bakabihindura imbyino. Kuri twebwe iyo tubyina, ni urwibutso rw’abakurambere, imibereho yabo. Kuba bifatwa nk’imbyino gusa ntabwo ari byo, kuko ni imibereho, ni urwibutso”.
